NOTE: 1) A negative reaction does not exclude the diagnosis.

 

 

 

 

 

           2) A positive reaction is one in which agglutination occurs in a dilution of

 

 

               more than 1/80 and rises with the duration of disease.

 

 

 

 

 

           3) A positive reaction with ‘H’ antigen indicates that Typhoid Fever is present

 

 

               or that patient had Typhoid Fever or has had vaccine.

 

 

 

 

 

           4) A positive reaction with ‘O’ antigen is more significant of infection when

 

 

               agglutination occurs in a dilution of 1/80 or more than 1/80
